text:
[TLSRec](https://yneversky.github.io/Papers/cikm22.pdf) supports dimension-wise local/global fusion: its sigmoid gate combines short-term, long-term and time-lag embeddings, then forms g⊙short+(1−g)⊙long. Replacing the gate with averaging lowers Hit@20 from 0.3438 to 0.2989 on Amazon Book and 0.2423 to 0.1702 on Amazon Video. However, this is session-based convex fusion, not h+g⊙Wr; it does not establish an optimal five-item window, gate initialization or normalization placement for the proposed residual.

[SASRec’s original implementation](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/model.py) scales input item embeddings by √d, applies normalization within blocks and at the final sequence output, and scores against the tied embedding table. Thus, distinguish raw tied embeddings from scaled Transformer inputs when constructing r. Engineering inference: start with a small residual using small gate weights and bias around −2 (sigmoid≈0.12), or a small projection; zeroing W exactly initially blocks the gate’s gradient. Measure ‖g⊙Wr‖/‖h‖ rather than assuming compatible scales. Preserve SASRec’s normalization initially; compare branch normalization separately, since normalization after addition also changes the baseline representation.

[Fossil](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.09152) demonstrates effective sparse recommendation using similarity plus weighted recent-item transitions; [SASRec](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781) also finds stronger recency focus on sparse datasets. These motivate controlled comparisons: unchanged SASRec, last-item residual, ungated five-item mean residual, learned scalar residual and vector-gated mean, keeping projection, scale and training budget comparable. Mask padding and divide by valid count over positions t−4…t. Select using the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10; published results do not establish that the more complex gate wins here.
